newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The countdown for Albanian President Sali Berisha has begun as fears of a confrontation between north and south grow. The rebels concentrated in the south have kept up their calls for Berisha's resignation and vowed they would not hand over their guns.
--The moment of truth for the eight-week teachers' strike appears to be tomorrow, when an Athens court rules on whether the strike is illegal and an abuse of privilege.
--Thousands of property owners will be called on to pay more tax with the finance ministry's move to reduce the taxable threshold for own residences from 200 sq.m to 150.
--Two gold and one silver medal took Greece to fifth place overall at the Paris athletics championships over the weekend.
--Although the government was hoping for insurance premium increases of between 10-12 percent, some 67 Greek and foreign firms have produced new lists with increases of up to 50 percent.
--The centre-left government in Italy wants Greece to not play any role in Albania, according to reports, following Italy's successful brokering of a deal with rebels in Vlore to lay down their guns.

--Cheaper loans from banks are on the way, according to statements from four major banks. The reduction on lending interest is considered a certainty after the news that CPI inflation continues to fall.
--The first of this year's expected 11 million tourists and 500 million dollars in inflows arrived in Crete over the weekend. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
